somnath.name: Shree Somnath Jyotirlinga
somnath.tagline: The Eternal Shrine by the Arabian Sea
somnath.description: Somnath is revered as the first amongst the twelve holy Jyotirlinga shrines of Lord Shiva. Perched on the Arabian Sea coast, the temple stands as a glorious testament to faith, having been reconstructed in grand Chalukya architecture with intricate stone carvings, the sacred Banstambh, and a timeless spiritual aura.
somnath.historicalSignificance: Mentioned in the Rigveda and Skanda Purana, Somnath is known as the 'Shrine Eternal'. The current grand Kailash Mahameru Prasad temple was reconstructed under the vision of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and inaugurated by Dr. Rajendra Prasad in 1951.

dwarka.name: Shree Dwarkadhish Jagat Mandir
dwarka.tagline: The Sacred Kingdom of Dwarkadhish & Char Dham Shrine
dwarka.description: Dwarka is one of the foremost Char Dham pilgrimage destinations in Hinduism and a sacred Sapta Puri city. The grand Jagat Mandir rises with 72 intricately carved pillars and its iconic 52-yard sacred flag flying high above the confluence of the holy Gomti River and the Arabian Sea.
dwarka.historicalSignificance: Established over 2,500 years ago, Jagat Mandir is a magnificent 5-storied limestone structure with two sacred gateways — Swarga Dwar and Moksha Dwar.

ambaji.name: Shree Arasuri Ambaji Mata Temple
ambaji.deity: Maa Amba (Principal 51 Shaktipeeth - Heart of Sati)
ambaji.tagline: Supreme Shaktipeeth of Gujarat on the Holy Arasur Hills
ambaji.description: Ambaji is one of the 51 holy Shaktipeeths, revered as the sacred place where the heart of Devi Sati fell. Nestled in the picturesque Arasur hills near Mount Abu border, it is a spiritual epicentre for millions of Shakti devotees.
ambaji.historicalSignificance: Uniquely, the temple enshrines the sacred Viso Yantra with no anthropomorphic idol, maintaining centuries of Vedic Tantric tradition.

pavagadh.name: Shree Mahakali Mata Mandir, Pavagadh
pavagadh.deity: Maa Mahakali (Supreme Shaktipeeth & UNESCO Hill Complex)
pavagadh.tagline: The Sacred High-Altitude Cliff Peak of Champaner-Pavagadh
pavagadh.description: Perched atop the dramatic 762-meter volcanic Pavagadh peak, this ancient Shaktipeeth is dedicated to Goddess Mahakali. Pilgrims ascend via traditional stone steps or the state-of-the-art Udan Khatola (ropeway).
pavagadh.historicalSignificance: Dating back to the 10th-11th century, it is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, featuring a golden sanctum shikhara.
